There are both branched and unbranched forms here which are transparent, colorless, flat or cylindrical filaments. Extended description: Algae are unicellular or colonial aquatic plants. There are about 18,000 species, both marine and freshwater, in many shapes and forms. This sample consists of dried, powdered lake algae. There are both branched and unbranched forms here which are transparent, colorless, flat or cylindrical filaments. They are about 1 µm wide; most are 10-50 µm long, and show first-order grays and white (001001, 001011). Rounded forms are various diameters (<l to 100+ µm); most here are 8-10 µm . They are transparent, colorless, isotropic (000000), or show gray interference colors (001000). Algae include the diatoms (4) q.v. (000010, 000011, 010010, 010011). Any of the above may have colored pigment inclusions of green, blue-green, red, brown; either rounded (010000) or rod shaped (010001). In addition to the algae, this sample contains calcite (133), feldspar, quartz (183), biotite (167), clay, encysted protozoans, settled combustion products, and miscellaneous plant and animal tissue remains in various states of dehydration and decomposition.

microscopy description: Single cells may also be present, but one more frequently sees sheets of individual cells. The transparent, colorless to light tan sheets (001010, 011010) sometimes have one or more folds. The surface texture appears soft and scaly. When dandruff is lost, a number of these other particles come away with it. Note the birefringent paper fiber (001001).
Extended description: Dandruff scales are made up of epithelial cells (3), q.v. Single cells may also be present, but one more frequently sees sheets of individual cells. The transparent, colorless to light tan sheets (001010, 011010) sometimes have one or more folds. The interference colors are very weak gray, not usually more than 100 nm retardation. The surface texture appears soft and scaly. Dandruff usually contains a great variety of artifacts, especially paper and textile fibers, because oily skin acts as a dust collector. When dandruff is lost, a number of these other particles come away with it. Note the birefringent paper fiber (001001).

Extended description: Epithelial tissues cover the human body and line the digestive tract. The cells are of several different kinds, but the most important are from the outer human skin. Skin tissue is stratified, with a basal layer of newly produced columnar cells. These pass successively outward, become flattened and are cornified by the time they reach the surface. It is this cornified top layer that scales off as dandruff (2), q.v., or as single epithelial cells. Cells from the scalp usually flake off in sheets. Individual cells or simple groups of cells come from the fingers and other parts of the body, or from weathered dandruff. They may be deeply folded on themselves or rolled up like scrolls. They are transparent, colorless or light tan, polygonal flakes (000010, 010010. The indices are about 1.53 and the interference colors, if apparent, are low (001010, 011010; the average cell diameter is 20 µm.
